proposal.summary: Incorrect billing import validation rules introduced since August are causing erroneous bill calculations, which increased dispute ticket volume (E-01) and produced more disputes for actual reads than estimated reads (E-03). Evidence shows dispute tickets doubled from June/July to August/September (E-01) and disputed bills are higher for actual meter reads than estimated reads (E-03); hypothesis H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE is supported by these data (E-03, E-10). The release includes monitoring dispute ticket volume (crm-tickets), validating bill calculation (billing-db), reporting findings to SH-BILL, and the remedy to revert the billing import validation rules to the pre‑August 2026 version (SR-R1). The DEFINE Gate resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS with the blocking item VOB-U-U1 deferred outside the release scope, so the gate allowed release with known limitations; thus the decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION. Known limitations are: the deferred VOB-U-U1 (specific rule change) remains open; dispute response times stay within the existing SLA (median ≤1.6 days, p90 ≤2.8 days) (E-06).
key_points: Problem: Incorrect billing import validation rules introduced since August causing erroneous bill calculations and increased dispute volume (E-01, E-03).
Established: Dispute tickets doubled (E-01); disputed bills higher for actual reads (E-03); rule change hypothesis supported (E-03, E-10, H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).
Released: Monitor dispute volume (crm-tickets), validate bill calculation (billing-db), report findings (SH-BILL), revert rules (SR-R1).
Why released: DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS with VOB-U-U1 deferred outside scope → RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION.
Limitations: VOB-U-U1 open; dispute response times within SLA (median ≤1.6 days, p90 ≤2.8 days) (E-06).
